dimensions.assessment: Directly impacts state child welfare agencies, all recipients of CAPTA and Title IV-B/E federal funds, courts handling custody matters, and parents, caregivers, and children nationwide.
dimensions.evidence: Any parent, legal guardian, caregiver, or child who is aggrieved by an adverse State action... may bring a civil action seeking relief

dimensions.assessment: Imposes profound changes on child welfare investigations, licensing standards, custody dispute rules, and federal funding eligibility, with mandatory financial penalties and personal civil liability without qualified immunity.
dimensions.evidence: qualified immunity shall not be available as a defense

dimensions.assessment: Involves withholding, recovery, and graduated penalty deductions (5 to 15 percent of federal grant funds) for state noncompliance under CAPTA and Title IV programs.
dimensions.evidence: For the first finding of such a violation by the recipient within a grant period, 5 percent of the total funds provided

dimensions.assessment: Broadly amends the Child Abuse Prevention and Treatment Act, the Social Security Act (Titles IV-B, IV-E, and Chafee program), and the full faith and credit statute for child custody determinations (28 U.S.C. 1738A).
dimensions.evidence: This Act may be cited as the 'Yaeli Martinez Child Protection Act'.

dimensions.assessment: Permanent statutory amendments affecting federal funding conditions, legal standards, and court jurisdictions nationwide.
dimensions.evidence: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, no payments shall be made to a State under this part for any amounts expended for sex-rejecting interventions.

missing_information: Total aggregate federal grant dollars affected across all participating states
importance_detail.rationale: The Yaeli Martinez Child Protection Act alters federal child welfare programs under CAPTA and the Social Security Act, adds restrictions on state use of federal funds regarding sex-rejecting interventions, creates a federal private right of action, waives state sovereign immunity in specific contexts, and modifies full faith and credit standards for child custody determinations.
